title: Chavín de Huántar
summary: Chavín de Huántar, in the Peruvian Andes in Ancash, is a ceremonial and pilgrimage centre that gave its name to the Chavín culture. UNESCO dates the culture between the 15th and 5th centuries BCE; another source gives 900 to 200 BCE. Stone-faced terraces and plazas surround an internal system of galleries, vents and drains, and carved works include the Lanzón, the Raimondi Stela and the Tello Obelisk.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO's short description says the culture developed between 1500 and 300 B.C. and its statement of value says the 15th to the 5th century BC; World History Encyclopedia gives 900-200 BCE for the Chavín civilization and the site 'in use for over five centuries'. Sources disagree; the span here is UNESCO's widest.

where.modern_name: Chavín de Huántar archaeological site, Huari Province, Ancash, Peru
where.historical_name: Chavín de Huántar, Mosna valley, Chavín culture

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it one of the earliest and best-known pre-Columbian sites and an eponym of an ancient South American civilization.
